verification_method.probe_artefact_check: No 429s were manufactured — lighthouse_audit and performance_start_trace do not hit the app rate limiter; backend returned normally. No scrollbar/overflow measurement involved. No guard redirect involved (routes /, /lessons, /login are public).

perf_family_audit_presence_scan.conclusion: The claim's '112 audits total, only cumulative-layout-shift is scored in the perf family' is literally true.

cls_is_not_in_a_performance_category.observation: cumulative-layout-shift is referenced by the 'agentic-browsing' category in every report — not by any performance category (there is none).
cls_is_not_in_a_performance_category.implication: CLS is produced but never aggregated into a Performance score; the claim's framing is accurate.

live_reproduction.conclusion: Reproduced independently in both modes. The 112-audit navigation-mode count matches the author's stated figure exactly; snapshot mode differs in count (88) because it analyses current state, but likewise has no performance category.

root_cause_verified_in_source.code: const categories = ['accessibility','seo','best-practices','agentic-browsing']; ... const flags = { onlyCategories: categories, ... }
root_cause_verified_in_source.tool_description_line_13: Get Lighthouse score and reports for accessibility, SEO, best practices, and agentic browsing. This excludes performance. For performance audits, run performance_start_trace
root_cause_verified_in_source.conclusion: The MCP integration hardcodes onlyCategories without 'performance' (and Lighthouse's default config is ignored once onlyCategories is set). The author's stated root cause is exactly correct — and the tool itself documents performance as intentionally excluded.

answers_to_the_three_probe_questions.is_the_evidence_real_or_a_probe_artefact: REAL. Independently reproduced live (2 Lighthouse runs + 1 trace) and confirmed at the source level. Not a 429 (no app rate limiter touched), not a scrollbar false positive (no overflow measurement), not a guard redirect (all three routes are public and loaded normally).
answers_to_the_three_probe_questions.is_the_severity_justified: LOW is defensible and if anything generous. This is a measurement-tool limitation on the audit host, not a defect in EngFlow. Nothing in the application is wrong; Lighthouse merely cannot produce a Performance score here because the MCP wrapper deliberately omits the category. INFO would be equally appropriate. It should NOT be escalated, and it does NOT excuse the absence of a performance number — the author supplied LCP via performance_start_trace instead, and did not invent a score.
answers_to_the_three_probe_questions.is_this_correct_behaviour_rather_than_a_: YES — it is correct/intended behaviour of chrome-devtools-mcp 1.9.0 (documented in the tool description). The only 'error' in the original write-up is calling it a finding at all; it is better framed as a recorded tool limitation. The author in fact framed it that way ('giới hạn của công cụ này' / 'I did not invent a score').

residual_uncertainty.none_material: Every checkable sub-claim (category set, 112 audits, absence of metrics entry, absence of LCP/TBT/FCP/SI/TTI audits, CLS-only perf-family scoring, the four CLS values, the LCP trace values, and the root cause) reproduced. No counter-evidence found.
residual_uncertainty.not_checked: The author's separate claim that /llms.txt and is-crawlable failures are non-defects was not part of this claim and was not independently re-verified here.
